doc.title: Bill Berry and Buster Cooper interviewed by Michael Woods, Los Angeles, California, September 3, 1995

title: Why Take the A Train and It Don't Mean a Thing connect with audiences
summary: Woods asks about two Ellington tunes; Berry says audiences recognize the piano intro and applaud.

story.theme_name: Duke Ellington and his orchestra, as others knew them
story.community_name: Duke Ellington: the band, the man, his men

blocks.x: Two tunes, tell us about these two tunes. Tell us about “Take the A Train.” Why is it every time that tune is played, all over the world, anywhere, it has immediate rapport with audiences?
And then “It Don’t Mean a Thing.”
The introduction. You don’t even have to get into the melody. You play the piano introduction and everybody starts applauding.
That’s Strayhorn’s tune, huh? Billy Strayhorn. Yeah. That’s something else.
You know it’s just one of those ones that everybody loves. I don’t know why. © Fillius Jazz Archive -8-
